pharm: Intermediate-acting benzodiazepine; positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor.
quick: Anxiety: 2-3 mg/day in divided doses (range 1-10 mg/day)
May be taken with or without food

summary: Lorazepam is an intermediate-acting benzodiazepine indicated for the management of anxiety disorders and short-term relief of anxiety symptoms. It is habit-forming and a Schedule IV controlled substance, carrying a boxed warning for the risks of co-use with opioids and for abuse, dependence, and withdrawal. Effectiveness beyond 4 months has not been established, and it should not be stopped abruptly.
indications: Short-term relief of symptoms of anxiety or anxiety associated with depressive symptoms
Insomnia due to anxiety or transient situational stress (single bedtime dose)

dosage.d: Initial 2-3 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses; usual range 2-6 mg/day
dosage.n: Daily range 1-10 mg/day; largest dose at bedtime

dosage.d: 2-4 mg as a single dose at bedtime

dosage.n: Adjust as tolerated; increased CNS sensitivity

dosage.d: Increase the evening dose before the daytime doses
dosage.n: Use lowest effective dose for the shortest duration

admin: Administer orally with or without food
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration
Increase gradually and increase the evening dose first to limit daytime sedation
Screen for opioid co-use and substance use history; document controlled-substance dispensing
Taper gradually to discontinue; do not stop abruptly
moa: Lorazepam binds the benzodiazepine site on the GABA-A receptor-chloride channel complex, enhancing GABA-mediated chloride influx by increasing the frequency of channel opening. This potentiates neuronal inhibition, producing anxiolytic, sedative, hypnotic, anticonvulsant, and muscle-relaxant effects.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to benzodiazepines or formulation components
monitor: Signs of dependence, misuse, and withdrawal

preg: May cause fetal harm; associated with neonatal sedation, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal with late-pregnancy or chronic use. Generally avoided; use only if clearly necessary and the benefit justifies the risk.
lact: Lorazepam is excreted in human milk; monitor the breastfed infant for sedation, lethargy, poor feeding, and respiratory difficulty. Weigh maternal need.
renal: Use lower doses and titrate cautiously; the glucuronide metabolite may accumulate in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Eliminated by glucuronidation (no oxidative metabolism), so it is relatively preferred in mild-moderate hepatic impairment; still use caution and lower doses, and avoid in severe insufficiency.

major: Opioids (boxed warning): profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death
moderate: Probenecid and valproate (raise lorazepam levels; reduce dose)
Sedating antihistamines and muscle relaxants (additive sedation)
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive CNS and respiratory depression with increased overdose risk.
interactions.diagnostics: No major laboratory test interference established.

monitoring: Level of sedation and psychomotor function
Signs of misuse, abuse, and dependence
Respiratory status if combined with opioids/CNS depressants
Periodic reassessment of continued need and taper plan
counsel: Habit-forming; take only as prescribed and do not increase the dose
Do not stop suddenly; the dose must be tapered to avoid withdrawal and seizures
Avoid alcohol and other sedatives; tell all prescribers you take this
May impair driving and operating machinery

pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light
pearls: Habit forming: Yes - Schedule IV; assess abuse risk before and during therapy
Metabolized solely by glucuronidation (no active metabolites), making it favorable in hepatic impairment
Avoid co-prescribing with opioids; if unavoidable use lowest doses and monitor closely
Flumazenil reverses overdose but can precipitate seizures in dependent patients
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is near the next dose, in which case skip it; do not double up. For regular anxiety dosing, maintain consistent timing.
overdose: Presents with somnolence, confusion, slurred speech, ataxia, hypotension, respiratory depression, and coma, worsened by other CNS depressants. Provide supportive care with airway and ventilation support and IV fluids; flumazenil may be used cautiously but can precipitate seizures and withdrawal in chronic users.
